course_name_original: Legislație in siguranta si protectia muncii

learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate knows the national legislative framework regarding occupational safety and health (Law no. 319/2006, Decisions no. 355/2007, 1093/2007, 1028/2006 etc.).
The student/graduate understands the methodological norms and legal obligations of employers in different sectors of activity.
The student/graduate is familiar with the basic concepts regarding risk assessment, legal responsibility in occupational safety and health.
The student/graduate understands the minimum protection requirements applicable to equipment and the work environment.
The student/graduate has the ability to interpret and apply specific legislation in real work contexts.
The student/graduate has the ability to identify and evaluate professional risks and to formulate prevention measures.
The student/graduate elaborates the necessary documentation for implementing legislative requirements in design, maintenance or operation.
The student/graduate uses legal procedures for implementing safety measures in companies and organizations.
The student/graduate assumes responsibility for complying with legal requirements in engineering activities.
The student/graduate actively participates in formulating internal occupational safety policies.
The student/graduate is responsible for documenting and applying legal norms to avoid sanctions and accidents.
The student/graduate has the ability to carry out evaluation and legal compliance activities with minimal supervision.
The student/graduate can independently manage a work plan focused on occupational safety.
The student/graduate can efficiently use legislative resources and documentation platforms for self-training and continuous knowledge updates.

syllabus_topics: Law no. 319 of July 14, 2006 (updated) on occupational safety and health
Methodological norms from October 11, 2006, regarding Law no. 319/2006 on occupational safety and health
Decision no. 355 of April 11, 2007, regarding workers' health surveillance

Decision no. 10935 of August 16, 2007, on establishing minimum safety and health requirements for the protection of workers against risks related to exposure to carcinogenic or mutagenic agents at the workplace
Occupational safety and health legislation. What obligations do we have as employers?
Legislation in the field of work and occupational safety applicable in Mechanical Engineering
Decision no. 1028 of August 9, 2006, on establishing minimum safety and health requirements regarding the use of display screen equipment
Decision no. 1048/09/2006 on minimum health and safety requirements for the use of personal protective equipment by workers at the workplace
Legal liability for health and safety at work
Law no. 126 of December 27, 1995, regarding the regime of explosive materials
Assessment of occupational accident and disease risks

assessment_methods.method: Mid-term test (multiple choice, 5 questions, in week 8)
Final evaluation (multiple choice test, 12 questions from course and project, 15 minutes)

assessment_rules: The result of the final evaluation for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of minimum learning outcomes and the granting of associated study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the Exam component (mid-term and final tests) and the Seminar component (active participation).
